name: Achish
bio:
Achish was the king of Gath. Fleeing from Saul, David at one point took refuge in Gath, but Achish's officials recognized him as the very David the women sang about — "Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands" — leaving David afraid. He pretended to be insane in front of Achish, scratching on the doors of the gate and letting saliva run down his beard. Achish said to his servants, "Look at the man! He is insane! Why bring him to me? Am I so short of madmen that you have to bring this fellow here to carry on like this in front of me? Must this man come into my house?" and had David driven away (1 Samuel 21:10-15). David escaped this danger and continued his years as a fugitive.

David later fled to Achish again at Gath, this time with six hundred men and their households; Achish gave him the town of Ziklag to settle in, and David lived in Philistine territory for a year and four months (1 Samuel 27:1-7). During this time David raided the Geshurites, Girzites, and Amalekites while falsely reporting to Achish that he had attacked the Negev of Judah; Achish, believing him, became convinced David had made himself utterly odious to his own people and would be his servant forever (1 Samuel 27:8-12). When the Philistines gathered for war against Israel, Achish had David march with him, even promising to make him his personal bodyguard for life (1 Samuel 28:1-2); but the other Philistine commanders distrusted David and insisted Achish send him back, fearing he might turn on them in battle to win back his king's favor by taking Israelite heads. Achish praised David as faultless and as trustworthy as an angel of God, yet had no choice but to yield to the other commanders and send David back to Ziklag (1 Samuel 29). Achish's consistent trust in David, set against the other commanders' suspicion, inadvertently spared David the impossible choice of fighting his own people.
